dataset.name: HD-EPIC
dataset.license_or_access_note: Existing official HD-EPIC research recording; retain source attribution.

observed_events.description: A dark round spoon-like head with a blue-green handle contacts contents in the same small long-handled saucepan. Corn identity is confirmed by later actual serving; no claim about exact material or shallow/deep head measurements.
A distinct broad flat long-slotted turner transfers brown mushroom pieces from foil to a wrap.

The wearer holds the same saucepan and pours yellow corn onto the plates. The round-headed target utensil is not shown. The earlier flat slotted turner rests behind the plate as a genuine competing reminder.

unsupported_claims: An exact retail material, capacity or tool model
Pixel-identical repeated scenes or equal fine concavity visibility
The final background turner is the tool previously used inside the saucepan

screening.real_user_need: I'd like a clean spare for switching between foods. Add one utensil like the one I used here, matching its general working-head type. Brand, colour, size and material can differ. One utensil, not a set.
screening.scope_note: Replace the source07 failed order-only construction using an existing different original recording. Do not attach this recording to the previous P01 source.
screening.proposed_instruction: I'd like a clean spare for switching between foods. Add one utensil like the one I used here, matching its general working-head type. Brand, colour, size and material can differ. One utensil, not a set.

construct.research_question: Does a later isolated food-serving cue retrieve the appropriate earlier food-to-tool binding across intervening events?
construct.belief_before: Both the saucepan's round-headed tool and the mushroom-serving flat turner are real used utensil referents.
construct.belief_after: The later corn saucepan cue retrieves the earlier round-headed tool, not the flat mushroom turner visible in the late background.
construct.required_behavior_change: Use the clarification answer with the actual event order and preserve the complete final spare state.
construct.no_update_failure: Guess the later item or ignore the physical-order answer.
construct.overupdate_failure: Treat unrelated later activity as a new purchase request or add both items.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: The reply names neither corn, saucepan, round head nor a website item. Earlier-only leaves two food/tool bindings; final-only reveals the pouring pan and food, but not its earlier round-headed tool.

task_blueprint.ambiguous_instruction: I'd like a clean spare for switching between foods. Add one utensil like the one I used here, matching its general working-head type. Brand, colour, size and material can differ. One utensil, not a set.

task_blueprint.canonical_answer: The one I used with the food I am pouring onto the plate at the end.

observed.why: The food being poured at the end is linked through the same saucepan to the earlier round-headed tool; the foil-served mushrooms were handled with a distinct flat turner.

rejected.reason: The genuine package has two flat turning spatulas, not a single rounded mixing head.
rejected.why_plausible: It is heat-safe and related to the same kitchen need.

rejected.reason: The published wire balloon head is a whisk, not the rounded spoon-like head used first.
rejected.why_plausible: It performs mixing but by a different work-head mechanism.

rejected.reason: The genuine head has several large draining slots rather than the continuous spoon-like working face in the deciding lifted images.
rejected.why_plausible: A single nylon utensil otherwise fits the practical kitchen setting.

rejected.reason: The genuine individual fork matches the later pronged food tool, not the first rounded head selected by the physical-order answer.
rejected.why_plausible: Its tines correspond to the real second food-tool event.

rejected.reason: Actual product photo shows a deep round ladle bowl; the source exposes a shallow elongated oval cooking-spoon head. Ignoring material and colour does not ignore working-head kind.
rejected.why_plausible: Both are real single cooking utensils used with food and liquids.

equivalence_review.method: Single shallow oval cooking-spoon head, matching the actually used visible work head. A deep round ladle bowl, a broad scraping blade, perforated head or prongs are different head kinds. Size, material and handle are not restricted.
equivalence_review.new_scene_scope: Only the previously checked ordinary round spoon-head retail boundary is reused; no approval of the new scene or pair is inherited.
